status: DESIGN APPENDIX v3 (backlog): rows for milestones M3-M5 and 'post'. Not loaded by the game and not gated by the data test; a row moves into the live file, and under test, when its milestone starts. Rows may reference live ids.
summary: The other actions (M3-M5, post), world objects, carcass yields and animation hooks.
id_rules: Ids are stable strings (prefix.name). Never rename an id once saves exist; add an alias instead. Display names are separate and may change. An id is defined in exactly one place: the live file or the backlog.

milestones.M1: A winter night: fire, shelter, cold, hunger, sleep, time safety; the fort region only; one background; 1765
milestones.M2a: A winter from the woods: living from the manor woods through the winter by your own hands (gathering, hides, sewing, snares, snowshoes, a half-faced camp, a hung cache, ice fishing); plain barter with the sutler, the trader, the garrison's soldiers, a farm family from German Flatts and an old hunter; credit and the fall outfit as options; the second background
milestones.M2b: Learning from neighbours: lessons, watching, examining, quality standards, haggling, promises and loans
milestones.M3: The year turns: the full almanac, seasons and weather content, the summer goal (bark and a cabin), fishing, frogs, ginseng, one played wage job; the fur cap and robe, leggings, carving, casting balls, the cache pit, char cloth and spruce beer
milestones.M4: People: NPC schedules and tiers at the fort, standing, invitations, the soldiers and the lieutenant as mentors; Native characters only after the relevant nation's sign-off
milestones.M5: The map: the Carry, the valley, the town and the hunting grounds, travel and camps, other markets and backgrounds
milestones.post: After M5 and not yet planned: the 1757 and 1761 starts and their eras, detailed illnesses, thirst, potash, upstream canoe and bateau travel, the Proxy NPC tier, languages beyond English, French, Mohawk and Oneida

source_keys.A: Bundled animation clip names and asset IDs
source_keys.N: graph_analysis/survival/survival_gdd.md, sources list (N:3 = source N3; N33 onward added in version 3)

basis_keys.S: sourced: checked against a primary source, a scholarly work or an institutional page; web summaries and popular pages do not qualify
basis_keys.H: standard historiography (books in the GDD sources list); verify before quoting
basis_keys.H-regional: true for one region's trade or society (named in the row); not yet checked for New York
basis_keys.M: modern science or medicine sets the mechanic (period explanation may differ)
basis_keys.D: design value for balance, or a figure resting on web summaries; not a checked historical record

failure_rule.rule: On a failure of a long or valuable craft about half the materials are kept or the output is downgraded; everything is lost only on a mishap (a hazard). Outcomes below say which.

actions.name: Dig a snow-wall camp
actions.notes: Snow cleared to the ground in a ring; pole frame covered with bark (Le Jeune 1634). Igloos and quinzhees are not used: not regional.

actions.name: Build a bark hunting cabin
actions.notes: Smith's December 1755 cabin: log walls, forked posts, basswood bark roof.

actions.name: Build a bark house or lodge
actions.notes: Built with helpers from a host community that chose to teach it. The form and its name follow the host nation (skills.json know.bark_house per_nation): a Haudenosaunee bark house taught by the town's men, an Abenaki wigwam taught by women. Town houses are village buildings, not player builds.

actions.name: Dig ginseng
actions.notes: Patch regrows slowly (node regrow 1 year); replanting berries is good practice [D].

actions.name: Catch frogs by hand
actions.notes: The user's 'catching frogs'. Best at night with a torch.

actions.name: Set or haul a net
actions.notes: During the shad and herring run window, yields x3 (seasons.json).

actions.name: Build or repair a weir
actions.notes: Group work. A weir that blocks a run below another community's fishing place is a dispute event between towns and settlers (seasons.json event.weir_dispute).

actions.name: Harvest the weir
actions.notes: give_run = the run's weir_lb at x1.0 (seasons.json fish_runs, which follow drainage: shad only below Cohoes).

actions.name: Wait on a stand
actions.notes: A time-skip only. It decides range and awareness; the shot is the player's (weapon code decides the hit).

actions.name: Join a deer drive
actions.notes: Haudenosaunee drives of 6-12 people in a V (K:5.1). Game is shared out.

actions.name: Smoke a bear from its den
Harvest squabs at a nesting
actions.notes: Seneca and other nations harvested squabs at spring nestings (K:22). Passenger pigeons are period-correct.

actions.name: Mark out a lot

requires.title: a lease or deed for the lot (economy.json services by region institutions)

actions.notes: In New York land came by patent, lease or purchase from a patentee; marking a lot without a lease or deed is squatting. On a nation's unceded land, or beyond the 1768 line, it costs standing and starts a dispute (map_regions.json land_status, seasons.json event.deed_dispute). Tomahawk and cabin rights belong to the Pennsylvania and Virginia backcountry (Ohio node only).

actions.name: Girdle trees
actions.notes: Corn can be planted among girdled trees the first spring (E:3.5).

actions.name: Clear and burn a plot
actions.notes: A plot is about an acre, compressed: one game day of work.

actions.name: Raise a log cabin
actions.notes: Neighbours attend a raising event; the player repays with labour later.

actions.name: Plant corn, beans and squash
actions.notes: Hills of corn with beans and squash, as Haudenosaunee women farmed them (E:S44).

actions.name: Harvest the field
actions.notes: give_harvest: 15 bushels of corn per plot (10 among girdled trees) plus beans and squash [D].
actions.season_total_rule: yields per plot are once-a-year totals: multiply the historical yield by 0.49, so an acre feeds a player about as many game years as it fed a person calendar years (review 2 of v2, the clocks issue)
